analysis: The PR introduces compile-time BuildEnvironment (prod/dev) and a generated identity table. Production values reproduce the previous literals: keychain service io.darkbloom.provider.app-attest.shadow.v1, ~/.darkbloom, auth_token path and the lock-file directory. It was checked that prod behavior is unchanged in KeychainShadowKeyStorage.swift:12, WorkerCredentialLease.swift:11, AppAttestPreflightProbe.swift:67 and DeviceAuth.swift. Dev gets separate paths, ports, labels and keychain items, but shares the signing ID, access group, MDM profile IDs and the root fan helper (BuildEnvironment.swift:25-36). That gap is the one finding. The fan helper bumps helperVersion to 2 (FanIPC.swift:11) and adds compareHelperVersion, which returns nil on non-integer input. The XPC fallback encoding now uses the constants (FanXPCService.swift:126). The peer authorization policy, code requirement and root-only restore are unchanged. The per-session lease change described in the comment lives in FanDaemon, which is not in this batch, so the T-046/T-047 lease expiry and restore behavior is unverified. How callers use a nil compareHelperVersion result (downgrade or upgrade decisions, T-047) is also not visible. The dev coordinator default is api.dev.darkbloom.dev, and the dev build shares the production CDN and weights cache with its own revision ref. Next passes should check Package.swift and the release workflow for dev/prod publish separation, FanDaemon lease semantics, helper install/upgrade code, and any other users of the old hardcoded ~/.darkbloom paths.

findings.detail: The PR adds a second, team-signed 'dev' build (DARKBLOOM_ENV_DEV) that deliberately keeps the production code-signing identifier io.darkbloom.provider, the keychain access group SLDQ2GJ6TL.io.darkbloom.provider, and the root fan helper and its XPC code requirement (BuildEnvironment.swift lines 25-36). Only the keychain label/service prefix, install directory and port differ. Any dev artifact is therefore a same-team binary that already satisfies the fan helper's providerRequirement and has the entitlement to read the production SE key (label io.darkbloom.provider.attestation-signing.v2) and the production shadow-key item. Separation is by naming convention only, not by an access boundary. If the dev release pipeline or its signing inputs are weaker than production's, or a dev build is registered by mistake in the release or qualification registry (A-011, A-017), a dev artifact could reach production identity and root fan control. The same applies to the shared model-weights cache, where the dev build selects its own revision ref and falls back to production's. Fix: document this in TB-003, TB-010 and T-044, and ensure the dev workflow can never publish to the production registry or qualification path. Consider a dev-specific code requirement or CDHash allowlist in the fan helper.
findings.title: Dev/prod coexistence shares signing identity, keychain access group and root fan helper without threat-model coverage
